 Dated this the 6th day of April 2026
 Judgment

The appellant, who is the claimant in OP(MV) No.19/2012 of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Muvattupuzha [hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal'] has filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

2. On 10.11.2011 at 6.10 p.m while the claimant was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-17/F 9049 through Muvattupuzha-Perumbavoor public road and when he reached at Pezhakkappilly, a lorry bearing registration No.KL-34/7009 driven by the 2nd respondent hit on the motorcycle and as a result of the accident, claimant sustained grievous injuries.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident his left leg was amputated.
Accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the 2 nd respondent, who was the driver of the offending lorry.
R1 is the RC owner of the said lorry and R3 is the insurer.
Hence the claimant 2026:KER:30381 approached the Tribunal seeking compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
3. Before the Tribunal R1 and R2 remained absent and they were set ex parte.
4. The 3rd respondent/insurance company filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy for the offending lorry.
But it was contended that there was contributory negligence on the part of the claimant in resulting the accident.
It was also contended that the amount claimed under various heads are excessive.
Further it was contended by R3 that since the lorry had no fitness certificate at the time of accident there was violation of policy conditions and R3 is not liable to pay compensation.

5. Heard the learned counsel for both sides and perused the records.
6.
It is an undisputed fact that on 10.11.2011 at 6.10 p.m the claimant met with a motor vehicle accident at Pezhakkappilly.

It is in evidence that while the claimant was riding a motorcycle, the 2026:KER:30381 lorry bearing registration No.KL-34/7009 driven by the 2 nd respondent hit on the motorcycle and in the said accident claimant sustained grievous injuries.
7. Ext.A5 final report filed by the investigating officer would show that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of R2, who was the driver of the offending lorry.

8. The appeal has been preferred by the claimant seeking enhanced compensation on the ground that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is inadequate, insufficient and meager and it is not a just compensation as mandated by law.

It was contended that the Tribunal failed to take note of the loss of amenities on account of the amputation of the left leg of the injured and it was further contended that the amount awarded by the Tribunal under all heads are meager and on lower side.
9. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurance company contended that the award passed by the Tribunal is just and reasonable and claimant is not entitled to enhanced compensation.

2 2026:KER:30381 10.
Exts. A6

to A8 and A11 medical records would reveal that the claimant sustained comminuted fracture both bones of left leg and he had undergone 29 days inpatient treatment at the hospital and his left leg was amputated below knee.
11. The claimant is a pensioner and he was aged 56 at the time of accident.
The Tribunal took his notional income as Rs.3,500/- on the ground that though the left leg of the injured was amputated following the injuries sustained in the accident, he is getting pension.
12. Pension is only a post retiral benefit and not an exclusive source of livelihood, as a retired person may still undertake gainful employment subject to his physical and professional capacity.
Claimant was aged only 56.
Therefore, his notional income is taken as 8,000/- per month for the purpose of assessing compensation.
13. Under the head loss of earnings, the Tribunal has awarded loss of earning for a period of 8 months calculated at the rate of 3,500/-.
As mentioned in the preceding paragraph, this Court has fixed the notional income as 8,000/-.
Accordingly, claimant is 2026:KER:30381 entitled to get an amount of 64,000/-[8000x8] under the head loss of earning during the period of treatment.
14. Under the head pain and sufferings, the Tribunal has awarded only a sum of 40,000/, which is on a lower side.
The pain and sufferings undergone by him in having his left leg amputated may be unbearable.
Accordingly an amount of 75,000/- awarded under the said head.
15. Under the head loss of amenities, as against the claim of 1,00,000/-, the Tribunal has awarded only a sum of 30,000/-, which is on a lower side.
Accordingly an amount of 1,00,000/- awarded under the said head.
16. Under the bystander expenses, the Tribunal has awarded only a sum of 4,350/-, which is on a lower side.
It is in evidence that he was hospitalized for 29 days.
A person whose leg was amputated needs the help of a bystander even after discharge from the hospital at least minimum for a period of 3 months.
Accordingly an amount of 30,000/- (7500x4) is awarded under the said head.
Under the head transportation charges, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of 3,000/-.

Taking into account the grievous nature of the injuries sustained by him, the case of the claimant that special conveyance was required for his transportation is found to be acceptable and therefore, his claim for Rs. 10,000/- under the said head is found to be quite reasonable.
Accordingly, an amount of 10,000/- is awarded under the said head instead of 3,000/-.
18. At the time of accident, the appellant/claimant was aged 56 years.
Therefore, 10% of the income is to be added towards future prospects (National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

If 10% is thus added to his notional income fixed by this Court, the amount would come to Chandran Nair vs Saji Mathew on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43026258/
3 8,800/- (8,000+800).
Permanent disability as per the medical certificate is 40%.
The Tribunal has taken his disability as 40%.
Since one of the leg had to be amputated, his functional disability is taken as 75%.
The victim was aged 56, the multiplier applicable to him is 9.
Accordingly, an amount of 7,12,800/- is awarded under the head compensation for permanent disability (8,800x12x9x75/100).
In the result, appeal stands allowed.

The compensation payable to the appellant/claimant is as indicated in the tabular statement here below:
Sl. Head of Claim Amount Total amount No. awarded by after  the Tribunal enhancement  in appeal 1 Loss of earnings 28,000/- 64,000/-
2

Pain and suffering 40,000/- 75,000/-
3 Loss of amenities 30,000/- 1,00,000/-
4 Bystander Expenses 4,350/- 30,000/-

5 Extra nourishment charges 3,000/- 3,000/-
6

Transportation charges 3,000/- 10,000/-
7

Medical treatment charges 2,47,482/- 2,47,482/-
8 Compensation for permanent 1,34,400/- 7,12,800/-
 disability  Total 4,90,232/- 12,42,282/-
 rounded to  4,90,300/-
Amount enhanced 7,51,982/- [12,42,282 - 4,90,300]
20.
R1 to R3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount as enhanced by this Court with 9% interest per annum from the date of petition till realisation.

The 3rd respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount in the Bank Account of the claimant within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment, after deducting the deposit if any already made.
Since there was a delay of 40 days in filing the appeal, the claimant will not be entitled to interest on the enhanced amount for the said period.

22. Since the offending lorry had no fitness certificate, after depositing the award amount, R3 insurance company is entitled to recover the amount from R1, who is the RC owner of the offending vehicle.
